requirement: When two readers share the same in-flight document request, aborting the first reader rejects it with AbortError while the other reader can still receive the document.
Document-cache TTL starts at successful completion; an entry is expired when now equals completion time plus ttlMs.
Queue order is createdAt descending with microsecond precision, then priority descending when createdAt values are equal.
An after cursor continues strictly beyond its anchor tuple even if the anchor ticket has been removed from the queue.
When one of two in-flight document subscribers aborts, it rejects with AbortError and the other subscriber remains able to complete.
A queue cursor can be reused when the same status set is reordered or contains duplicate entries.
Moving backward with before returns the nearest preceding tickets, presented in canonical display order.
A document read and a preview read of the same tenant, user, document ID, and locale share exactly one in-flight transport operation.
Mutating a nested object in one returned document does not change a later cached document read of the same identity.
A full queue page has nextCursor equal to null when no additional matching ticket exists after its last item.
Queue list rejects a cursor with an unsupported envelope version using code INVALID_CURSOR.
If one in-flight document subscriber aborts while another is active, the upstream transport signal must remain un-aborted.
After a document transport request rejects, a later read of the same identity starts a new transport operation and can succeed.
Queue order preserves timestamp differences smaller than one millisecond, placing the later microsecond timestamp first.
